question: The game of judo was invented in the year ____________.
solution:
The correct answer is __**The game of judo was invented in the year 1882.**__.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 __ 
• **Judo** is a modern martial art created by **Dr. Jigoro Kano** in the year **1882** in Japan. 
• The term "Judo" translates to **"The Gentle Way"** in English, emphasizing the art's focus on skill and technique rather than brute force. 
• Dr. Jigoro Kano founded the **Kodokan Judo Institute** in Tokyo, Japan, to teach and promote Judo as both a sport and a way of life. 
• Judo was developed as a refinement of **traditional Japanese jujutsu** techniques, focusing on throws, grapples, and submissions. 
• It became an **Olympic sport** in **1964**, debuting at the Tokyo Summer Olympics, further solidifying its global popularity. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 __ 
• **Development of Judo:** 
• **Dr. Jigoro Kano**, born in 1860, was an educator and athlete who sought to modernize martial arts by creating a discipline that combined physical education, mental discipline, and moral education. 
• Judo prioritizes techniques such as **throws (nage-waza)**, **pins (osaekomi-waza)**, and **submission techniques (shime-waza and kansetsu-waza)**. 
• Unlike many martial arts, Judo avoids strikes and weapon techniques, focusing on unarmed combat and using an opponent's strength against them. 
• **Global Popularity:** 
• Judo is now practiced worldwide, with millions of practitioners across various countries. 
• The International Judo Federation (IJF), founded in **1951**, oversees competitive Judo globally, organizing events such as the World Judo Championships. 
• Judo's inclusion in the Olympics in **1964** marked a turning point in its international recognition and popularity. 
• **Philosophy and Values:** 
• Judo promotes the principles of **mutual welfare and benefit**, along with **maximum efficiency** in the use of energy. 
• It emphasizes respect, discipline, and personal growth, aligning with its roots in traditional Japanese culture. 
• **Historical Context:** 
• Judo evolved from **jujutsu**, which was practiced by Japanese samurai as a means of self-defense. 
• Dr. Kano refined jujutsu techniques to create Judo, removing dangerous and outdated methods to ensure safety and accessibility for practitioners. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 
• **Modern Judo Competitions:** 
• Judo matches are conducted on a mat called a **tatami**, where competitors aim to score points through throws, pins, and submissions. 
• Scoring in Judo includes **Ippon (full point)**, **Waza-ari (half point)**, and **Yuko (minor score)**, with Ippon being the ultimate goal for victory. 
• Weight classes ensure fair competition among participants, making Judo accessible to individuals of different body types. 
• **Educational Impact:** 
• Judo is widely taught in schools and universities, especially in Japan, as a means of physical education and moral development. 
• It is recognized as a way to improve physical fitness, mental resilience, and social values. 
• **Judo Uniform:** 
• Practitioners wear a uniform called a **judogi**, consisting of a jacket, pants, and a belt that signifies rank and skill level. 
• Belt colors range from white (beginner) to black (advanced), with additional ranks such as dan levels for experienced practitioners. </ul
